turkey_specific_content: Very little, and none of it is in the article itself. The only Turkey-specific items are the ₺ prices in the upsell aside (removed anyway), the KVKK privacy link and Turkish wording in the cookie banner (line 115, also in menu.js; needs an EN privacy/cookie notice), and the Turkish date format '19 Eylül 2026 · 6 dk okuma' (line 77; becomes 'September 19, 2026 · 5 min read'). There are no cities, no timezone/DST content and no e-Devlet. The article is universal astrology content written in a casual second person ('sen'), which maps directly to English 'you'. The JSON-LD Article and FAQPage (lines 14-15) are Turkish and must be fully rewritten in English, with mainEntityOfPage set to the /en/ URL. Also needed: html lang='en', an EN canonical, and reciprocal hreflang tr/en/x-default. Following the user's instruction, the EN copy must not name or compare itself to any third-party astrology site.
rationale:
This is a pure static blog article (Yıldız Günlüğü). The body is about 482 words, about 614 visible words including chrome. It has no tool, no fetch() calls, no page-specific scripts and no Turkish strings in inline JS apart from 'Hesabım' in the login-state header swap (line 72). Translating it is trivial and carries almost no JS risk. That is its only strength. It fails the main phase-1 criterion of a client-side tool with unique value.

In English, 'venus sign' and 'mars sign' are high-volume topics, but the SERP is saturated by high-authority horoscope sites, women's-magazine astrology sections and big chart-calculator sites. Those pages offer per-sign interpretations for all 12 Venus and 12 Mars signs plus a calculator. A thin 480-word generic explainer has no per-sign content and no calculator, so it is very unlikely to rank for anything meaningful on a new /en/ section. Even the long-tail 'venus and mars signs' query is answered by much richer pages. The page also mostly funnels to paid Turkish reports (Aşk Haritası, Sinastri) and to TR-only pages. Once those are removed, the EN page has nowhere useful to send visitors unless EN birth-chart or compatibility tools exist.

Better path: make it a phase-2 item and rebuild it as a 'Venus and Mars Sign Calculator'. The ingredients already exist client-side. /astronomy.browser.min.js is in the repo, and zaman-makinesi.html (around lines 261 and 288-289) already computes Venus/Mars ecliptic longitudes with Astronomy.GeoVector + Astronomy.Ecliptic. Add a native date (plus optional time) input with no dogum-giris.js, show the Venus and Mars sign in English, and add 12+12 short English interpretations. That would be a genuine tool targeting 'venus sign calculator' / 'mars sign calculator' (very high volume, very high competition, but tools convert better than articles). The cost is new development and writing about 24 interpretations, not translation.

If phase 1 needs a cheap supporting article to interlink EN tools, this page could be included at low cost. On its own merits it should not take one of the 6-9 slots.
